data.body:
Goal:
Add the visibility layer: each peer's last-seen time, version skew, and
recent failures are recorded locally and surfaced via `thimble peer
status` and the existing `thimble doctor`. Heartbeats are pull-based
("am I able to reach you?"); they record state but do NOT trigger
catch-up automatically (an operator decides what to do when a peer is
unreachable).

Verification:
1. New file `secrets/.peer-state.json` (gitignored, local-only, mode 0640) records per-peer: name, last_seen (RFC3339), last_error (string|null), version_skew (int — how far ahead/behind their manifest version was at last contact).
2. New subcommand `thimble peer ping [<name>]` runs an SSH no-op (`ssh <target> "true"`) plus reads the peer's manifest version via rsync, updates .peer-state.json, prints a one-line status.
3. New subcommand `thimble peer status` reads .peer-state.json and prints a tabular view: name | target | last_seen | version_skew | last_error.
4. `thimble doctor` (K-29) gains a "peers" check that calls into peer status: ok if all peers contacted in the last hour, warn if any contacted >1h ago, fail if any never contacted or last_error is non-null.
5. Optional cron-friendly: `thimble peer ping --all --quiet` for use in scheduled jobs (cron every 5 min). Document this in README.
6. Tests: stub the ssh+rsync; verify state-file updates, status output, doctor integration.

Constraints:
- Knot ref: K-57; depends on K-56.
- Files: internal/peer/heartbeat.go (new), internal/peer/state.go (new), internal/cli/run_peer.go (extension), internal/doctor/check_peers.go (new).
- Heartbeats are NOT a daemon. Operator runs `thimble peer ping --all` from cron, or implicitly via `thimble peer status` reads (which can be configured to refresh stale entries).
- .peer-state.json must be add to .gitignore (defensive, even though we're not using git as transport — operators may still have the secrets/ dir under git for backup of *encrypted* artifacts).
- Notes: this knot does NOT do automatic catch-up. If peer-state shows alice is 100 versions behind, it's the operator's call to manually `peer join` or rsync-replace. Auto-catch-up is a future knot.
data.title: Peer heartbeats and status reporting
